$comment: M13. The recap's frame: its opening line (open, off the recap deck, which may export a figure the close brings back; or sheet text of its own) and its closing line, before the engine's next step. The body is the engine's: when and how, whose evening is whose, who nobody has placed. The frame names nobody, no hour, no place (the correspondence check holds it to that). Flags: trigger (hour, lie, window, confront, link, demand), n (recaps so far tonight), tier, caseType, callback. The close: callback lines bring {figure} (or {mark}) back; plain lines need none; the engine's plain close is the recap deck's closing card. Every part is said in the opening paragraph, wherever it sits round the body; keep the opening and the closing line short (the recap is 80–180 words in all).

sheets.name: Taking stock
sheets.notes: The camp golden §4: the recap deck's opening line, the notebook, the deck's closing line; on a callback page the opening's own phrase comes back.

sheets.name: A clean page
sheets.notes: He writes it out fresh instead of reading it back; the page comes back at the end.

parts.text: I turned to a clean page and wrote out what I had, in order, the way they teach you and nobody does it.
alt: I found a clean page and wrote it all out again, start to finish, like a man with a plan.
I started a clean page. Writing it out fresh is the nearest I get to thinking.
I gave it a clean page of its own, which is more than I usually give anything.

callback: It didn’t fill {mark}. There was room at the bottom for the rest, whenever the rest turned up.
I read {mark} over twice. It didn’t get any longer.
{Mark} looked tidier than the night did. Neat handwriting will do that.
plain: That was the lot, in order. Order is the one thing I can always supply.
I read it back once and put the pencil behind my ear, where it does its best work.
Written out, it looked tidier than it felt.
That was all of it, written out neat. Neat is something.

sheets.name: My feet
sheets.notes: He sits down to take stock, and his feet get the last word before the next step.

parts.text: I found somewhere to sit and gave my feet a rest while my head did the walking.
alt: I got off my feet for a minute. They’d earned it more than I had.
I took the weight off my feet and let my head carry the rest.
I sat down, and my feet stopped complaining long enough for me to think.

callback: {Figure} had heard all of this before. They were ready to go, and so, more or less, was I.
I stood up. {Figure} filed a complaint, which I noted and ignored.
{Figure} had had their minute’s rest and wanted it known that a minute was not enough.
plain: That was the lot. I stood up, which my feet took personally.
That was all I had. My feet voted to stay, and were outvoted.
That was the lot. Getting up again was the hardest part of it.
I got up before I could get comfortable. Comfortable is where I do my worst thinking.

sheets.name: Again
sheets.notes: A second recap or later: the notebook read over again, which is getting to be a habit.

parts.text: I got the notebook out again. We were getting to know each other.
alt: Out came the notebook again. It was starting to expect me.
I read the notebook over again. It had stopped being surprised.
Back to the notebook. We were starting to finish each other’s sentences.

callback: I put {mark} away. It had more in it than last time, and it looked about as tired as I did.
{Mark} went back in my pocket, a page heavier than before.
I closed {mark} gently. We’d both had a long night.
plain: That was where it stood, a little further along than last time. I’ll take further along.
Every time I read it over, it got a little longer. Some nights that’s the whole job.
I read it through once more for luck. It came out the same, which is what you want from a notebook.
It was more than I’d had the last time I looked. Not a lot more, but I’m not proud.
